sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A standing wooden figure with a helmet-like headdress, scarified face, aluminium eyes, and tapering openwork body — a classic Jukun ancestor/spirit figure type, and the museum explicitly attributes production to the Jukun.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A standing wooden figure with conical headdress, elongated cylindrical body pierced with openwork, and inlaid eye, consistent with Jukun ancestor/spirit figures used in ritual contexts; museum records it as made by Jukun.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing male figure, consistent with Jukun ancestor/spirit figures used in ritual contexts; the museum directly attributes it to Jukun makers.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A wooden mask with horns, carved for ritual use, matches Jukun mask-making traditions with animal-horned helmet masks used in masquerades.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A hand-woven narrow strip cloth in cotton with indigo and magenta silk supplementary-weft patterning, attributed by the museum to Jukun weavers—a classic Nigerian narrow-strip textile consistent with Jukun production.

textile.name: wrapper
textile.title: wrapper
textile.reason: A strip-woven cotton wrapper (kyadze cloth) with indigo and supplementary weft float patterns, explicitly attributed by the museum to Jukun makers — a classic Jukun textile form.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A handwoven narrow-strip cotton and silk cloth with indigo and magenta supplementary-weft patterning, explicitly attributed to Jukun makers by the museum — a typical Nigerian narrow-strip textile consistent with Jukun production.

textile.name: cloth; garment
textile.title: cloth; garment
textile.reason: A handwoven strip-cloth wrapper (kyadze) with supplementary-weft float patterning and embroidered border panels, explicitly attributed to the Jukun; this is a classic Nigerian narrow-strip woven textile consistent with Jukun weaving traditions.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A hand-woven cotton strip cloth with supplementary weft banding, directly attributed to the Jukun by the museum's production notes, consistent with Nigerian narrow-strip weaving traditions.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A hand-woven strip-weave cotton and silk textile with indigo and magenta supplementary-weft patterning, consistent with Jukun narrow-strip cloth production in Nigeria; strip weaving for larger cloths is a known Jukun craft.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: A hand-woven strip cloth of cotton and silk with indigo and magenta banded stripes, explicitly attributed to Jukun makers by the museum — consistent with West African narrow-strip weaving traditions.

instruments.name: dance-rattle
instruments.title: dance-rattle
instruments.reason: An ankle dance-rattle made of woven palm leaf segments strung together, a plausible musical/percussion accessory worn for dance by Jukun or neighboring Nigerian peoples; no evidence against the attribution.

arms.name: ceremonial axe
arms.title: ceremonial axe
arms.reason: This is a ceremonial axe/hoe with brass fittings and a crested human-head finial, explicitly attributed by the museum to the Jukun of Nigeria; such ceremonial staffs/axes are documented Jukun prestige objects.

arms.name: ceremonial axe
arms.title: ceremonial axe
arms.reason: A ceremonial metal-headed axe with decorative crescent blade, human/animal figural head, and long carved shaft with bell pendant, attributed by the museum to Jukun makers — a plausible Nigerian ceremonial weapon type.
